simple: the promise between whoever starts a kernel and the kernel: where it is loaded, in which CPU mode it starts and which register holds what.
analogy: how the caretaker hands over the building on the first morning: a folder of forms, or a plan of the building left on the desk.
precise: the entry state defined by a boot protocol: Multiboot (32-bit protected mode, eax = 0x2BADB002, ebx = information structure), the arm64 Image protocol (x0 = devicetree physical address) or OpenSBI's hand-off (S-mode, a0 = hart ID, a1 = devicetree address).
source: D5, D6 and D7 of BR-06 (RISC-V SBI Specification; Multiboot Specification; "Booting AArch64 Linux") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); entry values measured in BR-06 run R1

simple: the size of the smallest page an MMU translates.
analogy: the size of one locker on the locker map: the same wall with bigger lockers holds fewer of them.
precise: on AArch64 the translation granule (4, 16 or 64 KiB) is chosen by the kernel among those the CPU implements; x86-64 and RISC-V Sv39 use 4 KiB base pages. Core code takes the page size from the arch layer instead of a constant.
source: D3 of BR-06 (Arm Architecture Reference Manual for A-profile architecture) and curriculum 9.2 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: whether the C++ type char holds -128..127 or 0..255.
analogy: two schools that agree on the alphabet but not on whether the last letters count as "minus".
precise: implementation-defined by the language and fixed by each platform's ABI; in BR-06's toolchains plain char is signed on x86-64 and unsigned on AArch64 and RISC-V Linux (run R3). Portable code uses unsigned char for bytes and int for getchar results.
source: D15 of BR-06 (ISO/IEC 14882 and the processor ABI supplements) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); measured in BR-06 run R3

simple: an instruction that tells the data cache to write a line back to memory, or to forget it.
analogy: before the delivery truck takes boxes from the storeroom, someone carries the boxes still on the classroom tables to the storeroom.
precise: clean, invalidate and clean-and-invalidate by address: DC CVAC, DC IVAC, DC CIVAC (followed by DSB) on AArch64; cbo.clean, cbo.inval, cbo.flush from Zicbom on RISC-V; CLFLUSH on x86. Needed around DMA with devices that are not cache-coherent.
source: D3 and D13 of BR-06 (Arm ARM; RISC-V Base Cache Management Operation ISA Extensions) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); encodings assembled in BR-06 run R10

simple: a tiny kernel that only prints what it found when it was started, then powers the machine off.
analogy: the principal's first walk round a new building with a notebook.
precise: in BR-06, a freestanding image per machine (one unchanged core file plus one arch layer) that prints its privilege level, the boot contract's registers and the devicetree magic, then exits through that machine's own mechanism (isa-debug-exit, PSCI SYSTEM_OFF, SBI System Reset).
source: BR-06 lab, runs R1 and R8
